{
  "subtype": "focus_inference",
  "implied_focus": "The nature/typology of recurring IT incident problems -- characterizing each ticket by what kind of problem it represents (category, affected component, symptom, scope, and recurrence).",
  "per_column": [
    {"name": "problem_category", "supports_focus": true, "rationale": "Directly types the problem (connectivity, email, database...), the core facet of problem taxonomy the query asks about."},
    {"name": "system_component", "supports_focus": true, "rationale": "Identifies the affected component (vpn, database, email_server), a sound facet for grouping recurring problem types."},
    {"name": "symptom_severity", "supports_focus": true, "rationale": "Captures the manifestation/symptom (connection_error, complete_outage), differentiating problem kinds beyond raw category."},
    {"name": "scope_dimension", "supports_focus": true, "rationale": "Describes breadth of impact (individual_user, company_wide), a coherent facet distinguishing systemic vs isolated problems."},
    {"name": "recurrence_pattern", "supports_focus": true, "rationale": "Explicitly flags repeated_component/repeated_user, directly operationalizing the 'recurring' aspect of the query."},
    {"name": "time_to_resolution", "supports_focus": false, "rationale": "An operational metric on the incident, not a facet of the problem type; peripheral to a problem taxonomy focus."},
    {"name": "assigned_to_completion_match", "supports_focus": false, "rationale": "A process/assignment-consistency check unrelated to what type of problem recurs; scatters the focus."}
  ],
  "focus_coherence": 0.82,
  "structure_quality": 0.8,
  "focus_actionability": 0.85,
  "rationale": "The majority of columns (problem_category, system_component, symptom_severity, scope_dimension, recurrence_pattern) converge tightly on one coherent, data-inferable focus: a multi-facet typology of recurring incident problems. These form a genuinely differentiated analytical structure at a useful granularity -- category, component, symptom, scope, and recurrence are complementary rather than restatements -- and directly enable the 'recurring problem types' investigation, which is actionable (e.g., prioritizing VPN/email/database recurrences). Two columns (time_to_resolution and assigned_to_completion_match) drift toward operational/process metrics that do not characterize problem type, mildly diluting coherence and structure. Overall the set clearly realises focus inference rather than being a generic grab-bag."
}
